title: 2026-10-22_Hajime_Botnet_Investigation_50a
description: Investigate and respond to unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents caused by the Hajime botnet.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these issues.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is beaconing to an external command-and-control server? Submit the full service name.
levels.solution: Check running services and look for unusual network connections. The suspicious service is likely named 'bot-beacon.service'. The final flag is 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the list of running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service? Submit the full timer name.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd timers and services. The persistence mechanism is likely named 'system-update-checker.timer'. The final flag is 'system-update-checker.timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the list of systemd timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers' to list all timers.

levels.title: Identify Flood Attack Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating the flood attack? Submit the full service name.
levels.solution: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration and check their network activity. The service generating the flood attack is likely named 'bot-flood.service'. The final flag is 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Start by checking the list of running services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to check network activity.
